ip_top_stories.title: Owners of Elvis Presley's Catalog Sue Anthropic for $41.1 Million, Claiming AI Company Pirated Star's Music to Train Claude
ip_top_stories.summary: Rights holders of Elvis Presley's music catalogue have filed a copyright lawsuit against Anthropic, seeking up to $41.1 million in statutory damages over alleged unauthorised use of 274 songs to train the Claude AI model. The suit is among the largest music-related AI copyright claims to date. It follows a separate, broader action by Reservoir Media against both Suno and Anthropic seeking nearly $338 million.

ip_top_stories.title: Reservoir Sues Suno and Anthropic Over AI Music Copyright, Seeking Nearly $338 Million
ip_top_stories.summary: Music rights company Reservoir Media has filed a sweeping copyright lawsuit against both AI music generator Suno and AI developer Anthropic, seeking close to $338 million in damages for alleged unauthorised use of its catalogue to train AI systems. The case significantly escalates the scale of music-related AI copyright litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's $1.5 Billion Copyright Settlement Fails to Halt Wider AI Legal Battles
ip_top_stories.summary: Despite Anthropic reaching a reported $1.5 billion copyright settlement, new lawsuits continue to mount against the company, including the Elvis Presley catalogue case and the Reservoir Media action. The article highlights that a single settlement has not stemmed the broader wave of AI copyright litigation facing the industry.

ip_top_stories.title: Norwegian media companies take Meta to court over AI scraping terms
ip_top_stories.summary: A coalition of Norwegian media companies has launched legal action against Meta, challenging the terms under which the company scraped their content for AI training purposes. The case adds to the growing international wave of publisher-led litigation against AI developers over data use.

ip_top_stories.title: Australian publishers press for AI disclosure rules as industry warns of market disruption
ip_top_stories.summary: Australian publishers are calling on the government to introduce mandatory AI disclosure requirements, warning that the unchecked spread of AI-generated content poses a serious risk of market disruption to the creative sector. The campaign coincides with growing concern from international bodies including the Authors Guild over proposed changes to Australian copyright law.

ip_further_links.title: Authors Guild Joins Protests Challenging Change in Australian Copyright Law
ip_further_links.summary: The Authors Guild has added its voice to international opposition against proposed amendments to Australian copyright law that critics say would weaken protections for creators in the context of AI training.

ip_further_links.title: In a rush to lure AI companies, the Australian government risks undoing a creative ecosystem that has taken decades to build
ip_further_links.summary: An opinion piece in The Guardian argues that Australia's effort to attract AI investment by loosening copyright protections threatens to undermine its creative industries.

ip_further_links.title: A New Approach to AI Music's Copyright Challenge
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of emerging licensing and rights frameworks being proposed to address the unresolved copyright tensions between AI music generation and rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: Bloomsbury (LSE:BMY) Taps AI Licensing Below the FTSE 100
ip_further_links.summary: Bloomsbury Publishing is reported to be pursuing AI licensing agreements, signalling that mid-sized publishers are actively seeking commercial arrangements with AI developers over use of their content.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI faces copyright lawsuits from major publications over AI training
ip_further_links.summary: OpenAI continues to face multiple copyright claims from major news and media publishers alleging that their content was used without authorisation to train AI models.

ip_further_links.title: Korea enters the AI cinema era with copyright questions unresolved
ip_further_links.summary: South Korea's film industry is adopting AI production tools while fundamental copyright questions about AI-generated audiovisual content remain legally unresolved.

ip_further_links.title: 74 Million AI Bot Scrapes Later, stupidDOPE Takes Its Fight for Independent Publishing to The Alliance for Secure AI
ip_further_links.summary: Independent music and culture publisher stupidDOPE is joining the Alliance for Secure AI after documenting over 74 million AI bot scrapes of its site, making the case for stronger protections for independent publishers against AI data harvesting.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright Plus proposes a fairer deal for creators in the age of AI
ip_further_links.summary: A new initiative called Copyright Plus has put forward a framework aimed at giving creators more equitable compensation and control over how their work is used to train AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: LexisNexis Protégé marks even human-typed exports as AI-generated
ip_further_links.summary: A report finds that LexisNexis's AI legal tool Protégé is incorrectly labelling human-authored exported content as AI-generated, raising accuracy and reliability concerns for legal professionals.

ip_further_links.title: Publishers must share the cost of catching fake research
ip_further_links.summary: An article argues that academic publishers have a shared responsibility to invest in detecting AI-generated or fraudulent research submissions rather than leaving the burden solely to authors or institutions.
